ei.title: The whole morning had been chaotic.

fullPassage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock failing to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she was met with endless security lines. Sophie kept glancing at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally felt at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.

questions.passage: The whole morning had been chaotic. Sophie's day began with her alarm clock ①<u>failing</u> to ring, which had thrown her into an intense rush. After terrible traffic, her taxi finally arrived at the airport, where she ②<u>was met</u> with endless security lines. Sophie kept ③<u>glancing</u> at her watch with each second feeling like an hour. Worried that she could not get to the boarding gate in time, she rushed through the crowds of people. Just then, she heard an announcement saying that her flight had been "delayed." Letting out a deep sigh, she finally ④<u>felt</u> at ease. With an unexpected hour to spare, she would have time to relax and browse the airport shops before her journey.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ felt → feeling. 'with + 명사 + 분사' 구문에서 each second가 '느껴지는' 능동의 상태이므로 현재분사 feeling이 와야 합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① failing: with + 명사 + 현재분사 구문. alarm clock이 울리지 않는 능동 상태 → failing 적절
✅ ② was met: 수동태. Sophie가 보안줄에 '마주하게 되다' → was met with 적절
✅ ③ glancing: keep + 동명사. '계속 ~하다' → kept glancing 적절
❌ ④ felt → feeling: with + 명사 + 분사 구문. each second가 '한 시간처럼 느껴지는' 능동 상태이므로 현재분사 feeling이 필요합니다.
det.tip: with + 명사 + 현재분사(능동)/과거분사(수동). each second가 '느끼는' 주체 → 현재분사 feeling

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ said → saying. 현재분사 saying이 명사 announcement를 수식합니다. announcement가 '말하는' 능동의 상태이므로 현재분사가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① thrown: had + p.p. 과거완료 형태 → 적절
✅ ② arrived: 과거형 → 적절
✅ ③ Worried: 과거분사구문. 주어가 걱정을 '느끼는' 수동 → 적절
❌ ④ said → saying: announcement가 '말하는' 능동이므로 현재분사 saying이 와야 합니다.
det.tip: 현재분사(능동) vs 과거분사(수동). announcement가 '말하는' 주체 → saying

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① whose → which. 앞 문장 전체를 선행사로 받는 주격 관계대명사 which가 와야 합니다. whose는 소유격 관계대명사입니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① whose → which: 앞 문장 전체(alarm clock failing to ring)를 선행사로 받아 '그것이 그녀를 서두르게 만들었다'는 의미이므로 주격 관계대명사 which가 필요합니다. whose는 소유격이므로 부적절.
✅ ② where: 관계부사(장소, the airport) → 적절
✅ ③ Letting: 현재분사구문(능동) → 적절
✅ ④ her: 소유격 + 명사(her journey) → 적절
det.tip: 주격 which vs 소유격 whose. 앞 문장 전체를 받으려면 which. whose + 명사 구조에만 whose 사용.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② endlessly → endless. 명사 security lines을 수식하려면 형용사 endless가 필요합니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① failing: with + 명사 + 현재분사 → 적절
❌ ② endlessly → endless: 명사 수식은 형용사. 부사 endlessly는 불가.
✅ ③ Worried: 감정 과거분사구문 → 적절
✅ ④ browse: 동사원형 병렬구조(relax and browse) → 적절
det.tip: 형용사 vs 부사: 명사 앞 = 형용사(endless lines), 동사/형용사 수식 = 부사(waited endlessly)
